reason: A measurement of the corona hood, a part with no PO or FLOPO class (the previous review rejected 'hood' as a generic part). The leaf examples are transcription errors.
Latin indivisus/indivisa (embryo, epidermis) and 'not splitting' mean not separated into parts: PATO:0002034 undivided.
'-tinged' means faintly suffused with the colour. config/botanical_colour_synonyms.tsv reads 'lavender' as a NARROW synonym of violet FLOPO:0988027, and the faintness belongs in the record.
Involucrate means bearing an involucre; 'leafy' describes the involucral bracts and can be annotated on them separately (leafy FLOPO:0991012 or leaf-like PATO:0002457).
Compares two dimensions of one bearer (height less than width, ratio below 1). The nearest term is depressed FLOPO:0991103, but 'much lower than wide' is better kept as a ratio.
A measurement of the mid-leaf lamina cells of mosses: bearer plant cell (PO_0009002) part of leaf, position median FLOPO:0991381, quality length PATO_0000122 with a bounded range (pattern 02/05).
As for 'median cells length', with quality width PATO_0000921 on the median leaf cells (PO_0009002 part of leaf, position median FLOPO:0991381).

A vague horticultural habit word (forming low rounded clumps) with no settled botanical sense. 'stem: mounding' shows it is not even read consistently; caespitose FLOPO:0991007 and mat-forming FLOPO:0991010 cover the clear cases.
'Pustulate-based' is an exact synonym of tubercle-based FLOPO:0991367, so this word negates it. The quality inheres in the trichome (PO_0000282) of the stated part.
Negation of revolute PATO:0001963. The degree 'conspicuously' is a qualifier for the record, not part of the class.
Lanciform = lanceolate; oblanciform is a variant spelling of oblanceolate, PATO:0002330.

Two values on two surfaces of the blade: adaxial surface flat (PATO_0000407) and abaxial surface keel-shaped (PATO_0002522). With only 4 statements, a rule is better than a sibling of plano-convex FLOPO:0991184.
A colour stated of a region of the petal ('basal purple patch'): region base of petal + purple PATO_0000951. If no region is given, blotchy PATO_0000329 is the fallback.
The colour belongs to the cross-walls of multicellular hairs, and there is no PO or FLOPO bearer class for a trichome septum. A term would combine colour and structure in one doubtful class.
The blade is punctate (PATO:0001512). The reddish colour belongs to the dots, not the blade, so it must not be added as a blade colour; keep it in the record text.

'Narrowed' maps to tapered PATO:0001500 (previous rule C172), and 'scarcely' denies it in substance. The example 'to scarcely narrowed' is the second member of a range and should not be read on its own.

'Semiherbaceous shrubs' are partly lignified plants: semi-woody FLOPO:0991309. PATO:0002352 herbaceous is about dying back, not texture, and the bracteole texture sense has no term, so the rule is limited to plants and stems.
A costa or midrib running out beyond the apex: excurrent FLOPO:0991162. 'Short' is the length of the projection and belongs in the record.
A growth process or event (buds or bulbils sprouting, root sprouts), not a quality of the part. Root suckering, where meant, is covered by clonal FLOPO:0991268.

word: subapical and apical teeth same size
reason: An equality of size between two parts (subapical teeth as large as the apical teeth), not a quality of one part. Equal FLOPO:0991102 would lose which members are compared.

label: subcostal
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being located close to, but not on, the costa or midrib of the structure that bears it.
reason: A standard pteridological position of sori, sibling of medial (sensu botany) FLOPO:0991299. No PATO or FLOPO term exists.
A metaphor for a caudex or short-shoot covered by persistent dead leaves or leaf bases. When the source says so, the content is marcescent FLOPO:0991181 on those leaves, not a quality of the stem.
A transcription fragment of 'tinged pale to deep rose/purple'; the colour is in the following words.
A colour stated of the apex of the part: the apex region (PO apex class or plant organ apex FLOPO_0985023) + red PATO_0000322.

label: tristichous
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being arranged in three longitudinal rows round the axis that bears it.
reason: Standard term for three-ranked leaves, scales and flowers. Sibling of PATO:0001952 distichous and FLOPO:0991369 polystichous.

label: villulose
definition: A villous quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's long, soft hairs being short and fine.
reason: The diminutive of villous, as strigulose FLOPO:0991091 is of strigose and puberulous of pubescent. No existing term.
Teeth, perianth bristles and seed scales that are weakly attached come away easily, which is the shedability sense of deciduous (generic). 'Attached to' PATO:0001667 is relational and adds nothing.
Broadly wedge-shaped: cuneate PATO:0001955. The breadth modifier goes in the record, as with other 'broadly' shapes.
Glands, hairs or scales spread sparsely over a surface: PATO:0001566 distributed (synonym scattered). It inheres in the glands or hairs, not the blade.
config/botanical_colour_synonyms.tsv maps 'wine red' and 'wine' to red FLOPO:0988001. 'Tinged' is the strength of the colour and belongs in the record.
